extracted.intended_audience: politically engaged readers, policymakers, and critics evaluating public proposals and fiscal/political projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing the practicality, justice, and consequences of public finance schemes, constitutional changes, and regulatory projects; emphasizes realism, institutional compatibility, and respect for rights. Targets evaluation of proposals (taxes, representation, regulation) rather than their partisan promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess sufficiency and accuracy of proposed revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: All that he bestows upon the nation, which it does not possess without him, and supposing it all sure money, amounts to no more than a sum of 300,000_l._ a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the actual size of proposed receipts against real needs; do not accept rounded or speculative sums without accounting. Compare the author's imaginary revenue to known revenues (example: 300,000_l. vs actual 450,000_l.) and check for omissions or double-counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hinging national fate on a single person's power or life
rubrics_metrics.description: So we are staked on four chances; his power, its permanence, the success of his projects, and the duration of his life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how fragile a plan is to changes in leadership, mortality, or a single individual's continued influence. Robust policy should not require multiple unlikely contingencies to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not deprive ministers of minimal means to perform duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A good man would hardly deny, even to the worst of ministers, the means of doing their duty; especially in a crisis when our being depended on supplying them with some means or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposals leave sufficient resources to allow government to function; withholding necessary means can worsen crises regardless of the actors' virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh long-term economic harms against short-term fiscal gains
rubrics_metrics.description: By this manoeuvre, he left our trade, navigation, and manufactures, on the verge of destruction... All this for want of 300,000_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess indirect economic consequences (trade, credit, colonies) before approving measures that produce modest immediate savings but risk large systemic damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove a tax before a replacement revenue is actually realized
rubrics_metrics.description: What! to take off a revenue so necessary to our being, before anything whatsoever was acquired in the place of it? In prudence, he ought to have waited at least for the first quarter's receipt of the new ... revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: legislate changes only after replacement receipts are demonstrably in hand, or have a credible, immediate source identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate proposals by magnitude, feasibility, and cost–benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: They must see the object to be of proper magnitude to engage them; they must see the means of compassing it to be next to certain; the mischiefs not to counterbalance the profit;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Is the objective sufficiently important? Are the means feasible? Do expected harms outweigh benefits? Require concrete plans and realistic probabilities of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider how proposals accord with affected parties' opinions and habitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: They will examine how a proposed imposition or regulation agrees with the opinion of those who are likely to be affected by it; they will not despise the consideration even of their habitudes and prejudices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must consider existing practices, local customs, and popular sentiment; disregard of entrenched habits can produce resistance and failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check consistency with prior establishments and institutional purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: They wish to know how it accords or disagrees with the true spirit of prior establishments... Such establishments are our great moneyed companies. To tax them would be critical and dangerous, and contradictory to the very purpose of their institution; which is credit, and cannot therefore be taxation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reforms do not undermine institutions' fundamental functions (e.g., taxing institutions whose purpose is credit). Respect the contractual and institutional framework that gives public benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid attempting one-size-fits-all uniformity in complex systems
rubrics_metrics.description: In the complicated economy of great kingdoms... an attempt towards a compulsory equality in all circumstances, and an exact practical definition of the supreme rights in every case, is the most dangerous and chimerical of all enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the heterogeneity of sectors (colonies, companies, regions) and tailor measures accordingly; uniform solutions risk destroying beneficial diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match mode of contribution to nature of the object
rubrics_metrics.description: Our trading companies, as well as individual importers, are a fit subject of revenue by customs. Some establishments pay us by a monopoly of their consumption and their produce. This, nominally no tax, in reality comprehends all taxes. Such establishments are our colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose fiscal instruments (customs, excise, monopoly arrangements, troop contributions) appropriate to the economic and political role of each entity rather than imposing inappropriate taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect property rights and public faith; avoid retrospective annulment
rubrics_metrics.description: The money was the voluntary, free gift of the Company; the rescinding bill was the act of legislature, to which they and we owe submission: the author has nothing to do with the one or with the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of ex post facto measures that nullify agreed dividends or contracts; legal retroactivity undermines public trust and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arbitrary or extra-legal processes in inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: A judicature was asserted in Parliament to try this question. But lest this judicial character should chance to inspire certain stubborn ideas of law and right, it was argued, that the judicature was arbitrary, and ought not to determine by the rules of law, but by their opinion of policy and expediency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and parliamentary inquiries should observe rule-of-law principles; invoking arbitrary tribunals to achieve policy ends is dangerous and illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require practical specificity, not vague generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: What do all these fine observations signify? Some of them condemn, as ill practices, things that were never practised at all. Some recommend to be done, things that always have been done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand concrete mechanisms, specific provisions, and operational detail rather than broad aphorisms or circular assertions that add little to policy design.

rubrics_metrics.name: When speculative projects may influence policy, state clear ends and realistic pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: As the author has stated this Indian taxation for no visible purpose relative to his plan of supply, so he has stated many other projects with as little, if any distinct end; ... It is also from some opinion that these speculations may one day become our public measures, that I think it worth while to trouble the reader at all about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposals are speculative but likely to be adopted, provide end-goals, instruments, and transitional arrangements; otherwise they risk confusing debate or creating false expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess logistical feasibility of distant representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The writs are issued for electing members for America... Some provinces receive them in six weeks, some in ten, some in twenty... A vessel may be lost... the Parliament has sat and business far advanced without American representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider travel times, communication delays, election timetables, costs to representatives, re-election cycles, and wartime risks before proposing remote parliamentary representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure representatives can be independent and economically able
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the most considerable provinces of America... have not in each of them two men who can afford, at a distance from their estates, to spend a thousand pounds a year. If their province pays them, they are American agents, with salaries, and not independent members of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating representation that requires paid agents or produces pensioners dependent on the crown; independence requires either widespread wealth among electors or arrangements that preserve representative autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware political timing and signalling effects of constitutional critique
rubrics_metrics.description: First, because he observes justly, that his scheme... can add nothing to the authority of the legislature; much I fear, it will have a contrary operation; for, authority depending on opinion... an idea circulated among the people that our constitution is not so perfect as it ought to be... is a certain method of lessening it in the public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how proposals or criticisms may erode public confidence in existing institutions; reform language and timing to avoid unintended delegitimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the scope and chain reactions of constitutional change
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he well considered what an immense operation any change in our constitution is? how many discussions, parties, and passions, it will necessarily excite; and when you open it to inquiry in one part, where the inquiry will stop?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate secondary debates, partisan realignments, and cascading institutional inquiries triggered by major reforms; incrementalism may be preferable unless the case is overwhelming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time large institutional reforms appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience shows us, that no time can be fit for such changes but a time of general confusion; ... Perhaps a time of the greatest security and tranquillity both at home and abroad may likewise be fit; but will the author affirm this to be just such a time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid proposing sweeping constitutional changes during active crises or hostile external threats; choose moments of relative stability or clearly framed transitional moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware politically-motivated temporary fiscal concessions
rubrics_metrics.description: The administration contended only for its continuance for a year, in order to have the merit of taking off the shilling in the pound immediately before the elections; and thus to bribe the freeholders of England with their own money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize short-term tax holidays or fiscal measures that coincide with elections as potential vote-buying; seek durable, principled fiscal policy rather than ephemeral political advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate complexity to the needs of the occasion; avoid needless multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations for the colony trade ought not to be more nor fewer, nor more nor less complex, than the occasion requires. And, as that trade is in a great measure a system of art and restriction, they can neither be few nor simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design regulatory regimes proportional to the problem: neither simplistic slogans of simplicity nor proliferating controls without regard to effect—adjust complexity to practical necessities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and correct regulatory excesses when discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of these regulations had laid an unnecessary restraint on the trade and correspondence of his Majesty's American subjects... This, in that ministry, was a candid confession of a mistake;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to repeal or amend rules that prove unnecessarily burdensome; candid acknowledgement of error preserves credibility and commerce.
